**Audience:** mid-level undergraduate hydrology students\
**Time:** 2–3 hours\
**Author:** Tao Wen\
**Provider:** SERC, Data and Model Driven Hydrology Education

The [SERC teaching activity](https://serc.carleton.edu/hydromodules/units/191769.html) uses online observations to examine stream chemistry around brine-disposal locations in Pennsylvania. It also introduces questions about earthquakes and disposal of waters produced during oil and gas extraction.

Students compare water chemistry upstream and downstream, investigate possible explanations for seismic events, and use public records to examine brine disposal. The activity develops data-analysis, interpretation, and synthesis skills.

## Access and teaching

[Open the activity and lesson steps](https://serc.carleton.edu/hydromodules/units/191769.html).

The activity page provides instructions and assessment questions. Its listed tools include HydroClient, the Pennsylvania DEP oil and gas mapping tool, and Google Earth. Instructors should check these services before class and adapt the instructions if an interface has changed.

Cite the activity using [its DOI and citation information](https://doi.org/10.67165/cbzks996).
